- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive negative values), model underreacts to downward trend; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply 5–10% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.25), model exhibits high variance; use median of 5-day rolling forecast instead of 30-day projection.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion toward 65–68 range after 10+ days of high prices, model tends to hold high; apply 10–15% downward correction after 7-day high.
- Sentiment spikes to +0.3+ correlate with model overconfidence; reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment > 0.25 and price > 72.
